carouselA.title: Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: Taste becomes institutional knowledge only when people can examine how a judgment was made, practice it, dispute it, preserve its context, and retain authority over what may be carried.

frames.caption: 01 · ELICIT — What happened before “I just knew”?. Reconstruct the comparison set, sensory cue, memory, technical constraint, cultural reference, commercial condition, and rejected alternative. Record uncertainty and the contributor who supplied each part of the judgment.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what happened before “i just knew”? within Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · DEMONSTRATE — Can the judgment be shown in context?. Pair expert demonstration with a learner attempt, correction, second attempt, and commentary on acceptable variation. Some knowledge is tactile, temporal, embodied, confidential, or culturally governed; not everything belongs on camera.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping can the judgment be shown in context? within Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · CONTEST — Who can say the founder is wrong?. Create a review ritual where pattern, textile, production, wearer, commercial, cultural, accessibility, and archive perspectives can challenge a choice. Preserve the reason for override rather than manufacturing consensus.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who can say the founder is wrong? within Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · GOVERN — Who may retain and teach it?. Attach consent, compensation, attribution, confidentiality, access, teaching, archive, withdrawal, and cultural-authority fields. Keep protected expression, contract rights, trade secrets, know-how, and abstract taste as separate questions.

frames.caption: Turning taste into institutional knowledge can democratize learning, but it can also extract from workers, communities, and collaborators; privilege what can be verbalized; or make the founder’s preference an unquestionable rule. The system must preserve refusal, disagreement, privacy, and the right not to record.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for Can Taste Become Institutional Knowledge?.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery
